runtime_disclosure: On the current public Pages build, the RESIDUAL browser VM runs client-side with WebVM/CheerpX. Its writable guest overlay is stored in browser IndexedDB under an image- and guest-generation-specific cache identifier so ordinary reloads can preserve guest artifacts. Mission Control separately uses localStorage for browser-local conversation continuity: it keeps an index of up to eight conversations, restores at most the latest sixteen turns in a conversation, and can retain the latest accepted build bundle (up to eight text files, with per-file and total size limits enforced by the client). Session-scoped diagnostic state uses sessionStorage and is capped at approximately 1 MiB; it records sanitized environment, lifecycle, provider-stage and failure information and is downloadable by the visitor. A guest-generation identifier and service-worker recovery state also use sessionStorage. The browser runtime uses a service worker and browser caches as required for the VM. These browser-held records are not a hosted RESIDUAL account or server-side workspace. Closing a tab does not necessarily erase localStorage, IndexedDB, service-worker caches, downloaded evidence, or provider-held data. The public build removes WebVM's upstream Plausible analytics script and rejects eager Puter loading. Puter software is loaded only after the visitor chooses the provider feature; model calls then send the explicitly authorized prompt, selected source snapshots and bounded request context through Puter to the selected AI model service. GitHub Pages separately receives normal web requests and GitHub states that Pages visitor IP addresses are logged for security.
